study_identification_part.si4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research objectives with specific hypotheses. Criterion 1 (research hypotheses/questions provided): Satisfied - the authors explicitly state four goals and provide testable hypotheses. Criterion 2 (purpose of applying normative modeling): Satisfied - they describe using growth charts to identify atypical development and understand neural basis of affective impairments in psychosis, potentially informing prediction models and interventions.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Our goals in this study were 1) to identify the strongest age-associated changes in centromedial and basolateral amygdala connectivity in typically developing youths across multiple samples, 2) to characterize deviations from normative amygdala connectivity trajectories in psychosis, 3) to determine the specificity of these abnormalities by comparing age-associated amygdala connectivity in youths with other forms of psychopathology, and 4) to test whether age-associated deviations in amygdala connectivity are related to psychotic symptoms." Also: "Using neurodevelopmental growth charts to identify a lack of normative development of amygdala connectivity in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders may help us better understand the neural basis of affective impairments in psychosis, informing prediction models and interventions."
cm1_research_objectives.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md, Methods section (paragraph before METHODS header) and Conclusions section

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Criterion 1 (covariates such as age and sex considered): Satisfied - Age and sex were included as fixed effects in the linear mixed models. Criterion 2 (multi-site data methods described): Satisfied - Site was included as a fixed effect in all models, and the authors verified that including site as a covariate effectively accounted for site differences (residuals clustered around zero across sites with no significant differences).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Age, sex, and site were included as fixed effects." "Site, sex, and framewise displacement were included as fixed effects." "We also confirmed that site effects were appropriately accounted for by including the measure as a covariate. After regressing out the effects of site in each region, we then plotted the residuals. The residuals all clustered around zero, which provides evidence that we were able to effectively account for site in our model. Furthermore, when we conducted a mixed-model linear regression to compare residuals between sites, there were no significant differences between sites for any of the regions of interest (all x2=0, p=1)."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is performed in this study. Criterion 1 (preprocessing software specified): Satisfied - AFNI, FreeSurfer, and ICA-AROMA are specified. Criterion 2 (preprocessing steps mentioned): Satisfied - Detailed steps include: removal of first 4 TRs, warping to MNI space, normalization, 5mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing, Wavelet Despiking, bandpass filtering (0.009-0.08 Hz), nuisance regression (white matter, ventricular signal, motion parameters), ICA-AROMA motion artifact removal, and scrubbing. Criterion 3 (quality control procedures): Satisfied - Motion QC using FD and DVARS thresholds, volume censoring, and subject exclusion criteria are described.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The first 4 TRs from all scans were removed to allow for BOLD signal normalization. Functional images were warped into MNI standard space using a series of affine and nonlinear transforms... spatially smoothed using a 5-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel. Removal of non-stationary events in the fMRI time series was conducted using Wavelet Despiking... simultaneous multiple regression of nuisance variables and bandpass filtering at 0.009 Hz < f < 0.08. Nuisance regressors included were non-brain tissue (NBT), average white matter signal, average ventricular signal, six head realignment parameters... ICA-Aroma was implemented to remove motion artifacts... We censored and removed volumes that had an FD > 0.3 mm and/or DVARS > 20."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Criterion 1 (meaning and direction of deviation scores explained): Satisfied - The deviation score method is clearly explained: predicted normative value is subtracted from actual value, and the absolute value is taken to create a 'brain maturation deviation score'. The direction of effects (reduced vs. increased connectivity relative to normative trajectory) is discussed. Criterion 2 (quantitative thresholds reported): Not satisfied - No explicit thresholds (e.g., |Z|>1.96) are used to define extreme or atypical deviations. The deviation scores are used as continuous measures in correlation analyses. Criterion 3 (clinical implications discussed): Satisfied - Relationships with positive symptoms are discussed, including specific findings (r=0.19 for thalamus deviation-positive symptoms). Limitations of interpretation (small effect size, need for replication) are acknowledged.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "Using the model of best fit for developmental changes observed for amygdala connectivity in the typically developing control group, we predicted what the expected 'normative' amygdala connectivity value would be for the psychosis spectrum group. We then subtracted the predicted value from the actual amygdala connectivity value for each individual and took the absolute value of this score. This created an amygdala connectivity maturation deviation score." "Greater age-related deviation in centromedial amygdala-thalamus connectivity was significantly associated with increased severity of positive symptoms (r=0.19; q=0.05)." "Although this relationship was statistically significant after multiple comparisons, it is a small effect and must be replicated in future studies."
